title: Individual bounded-below truncation couples with natural comparisons
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] admitting derived categories and K-injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix $a\in\mathbf Z$ and let $\mathcal L_a$ be the set of derived objects $M$ with $H^r(M)=0$ for $r<a$. One can choose for every $M\in\mathcal L_a$ a type-zero bigraded exact couple $Z_M$ [def-sp-exact-couple], isomorphisms $e_D(M,n):Z_M.D^{0,n}\cong H^n(RF(M))$ and $e_E(M,p,r):Z_M.E^{p,r}\cong H^p(RF(H^r(M)[0]))$ for $p\ge0$, with $Z_M.D^{p,r}=0$ for $r<a$ and $Z_M.E^{p,r}=0$ for $p<0$. For every morphism $c:M\to N$ there is a couple morphism $T:Z_M\to Z_N$ [lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality] such that $T_D^{0,n};e_D(N,n)=e_D(M,n);H^n(RF(c))$ and $T_E^{p,r};e_E(N,p,r)=e_E(M,p,r);H^p(RF(H^r(c)[0]))$. No identity or composition law for the chosen maps is asserted and no coproduct is formed.

source.place: Canonical truncation triangles; Tags 015J and 05TC for the hypercohomology terms and truncation-to-abutment comparison. Steps 1, 3 and 4 of lem-pc-coproduct-truncation-couple, restricted to individual objects and morphisms.

proof.text: Choose strictly bounded-below representatives using DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE. Construct the exact couple with raw D, E, alpha, f, g from truncation_raw_exact. Transport the cohomological lower bound through homologyFunctorFactors and the representative isomorphism, and apply truncation_quadrant_vanishing. No additional injective replacement and no convergence data are used.
Use truncation_abutment_cocone for this explicit couple to prove the canonical abutmentMap is invertible. Compose its asIso with RF and homology of the representative isomorphism to obtain eD.

Define singleIso explicitly by inverse bridge, the single-functor shift isomorphism, RF commutation with shifts and homology shift comparison. Compose it with the image of the representative cohomology comparison to obtain eE. These are existing natural isomorphisms, without the ordinary-derived-functor comparison.

For c:M -> N, conjugate by the representative isomorphisms and apply raw_naturality to get tD and tE and all raw squares. Assemble CoupleMorphism from the alpha, f, g squares; the g square is reindexed by eqToHom_naturality for the zero bidegree. Compose the abutment square with RF homology of the representative isomorphism and cancel inverse/hom factors. For E, cancel homologyFunctorFactors and the representative inverse/hom factors inside homologyMap, then apply the single/RF/homology composite functor. This proves both displayed comparison equations.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_natural_boundedBelow_truncation_couples
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{v} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (a : ℤ) :
    let L := {M : DerivedCategory A // ∀ r : ℤ, r < a →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj M)}
    ∃ (Z : L → BigradedExactCouple B 0)
      (eD : ∀ (M : L) (n : ℤ), (Z M).D 0 n ≅
        (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj M.val)
      (eE : ∀ (M : L) (p : ℕ) (r : ℤ), (Z M).E p r ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj M.val)),
      (∀ (M : L) (p r : ℤ), r < a → IsZero ((Z M).D p r)) ∧
      (∀ (M : L) (p r : ℤ), p < 0 → IsZero ((Z M).E p r)) ∧
      ∀ (M N : L) (c : M.val ⟶ N.val),
        ∃ T : BigradedExactCouple.CoupleMorphism (Z M) (Z N),
          (∀ n : ℤ, T.tD 0 n ≫ (eD N n).hom = (eD M n).hom ≫
            (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map c) ∧
          (∀ (p : ℕ) (r : ℤ), T.tE p r ≫ (eE N p r).hom = (eE M p r).hom ≫
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
              DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).map
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).map c))
